client: MarketScope Analytics (fictional client from the capstone brief)
disclaimer: Simulated competitive-intelligence scenario. The three 'competitors' are public web-scraping sandboxes that explicitly permit automated collection (books.toscrape.com, webscraper.io test shop, web-scraping.dev). Their prices, ratings and reviews are demo data published by those sites (Books to Scrape states its prices and ratings were randomly assigned); review excerpts are the sandbox's sample reviews, not real customer feedback. The analysis demonstrates the method and must not be read as statements about real products or markets.

data_sources.access_basis: Public sandbox built for scraping practice ('This is a demo website for web scraping purposes'); no robots.txt (HTTP 404 = no restrictions under RFC 9309). Prices and ratings are randomly assigned by the site.

Public e-commerce test site provided for scraping practice. robots.txt only disallows /test-sites/product/, /test-sites/pagination/, /test-sites/scroll/ and /test-sites/load-more/; the static e-commerce catalogue used here is allowed.

Scrapfly's public scraping sandbox. robots.txt disallows only /robots-disallowed for all agents and sets Crawl-delay: 2, which the scraper honours. Reviews are the sandbox's sample reviews embedded in the product page (first page only; the CSRF-protected review API is deliberately not used).

methodology.pipeline: Requests + BeautifulSoup scraping -> pandas cleaning/validation -> deterministic same-currency price benchmark -> OpenAI Chat Completions with strict JSON Schema -> CSV/JSON export

cleaning_policies.deduplication: Duplicates are removed with pandas drop_duplicates inside each source only: (1) same source and canonical product URL (scheme/host lower-cased, #fragment and utm_*/click-id tracking parameters removed); (2) same source with identical normalised title, price, currency and description listed under different URLs. The most complete record is kept (ties: earliest scraped_at). The same title sold by different competitors, or by the same competitor at a different price, is kept as separate products.
cleaning_policies.missing_values: Empty strings and null markers ('N/A', 'none', 'null', '-', NaN) become real nulls. Records without a product name, a source or a valid absolute http(s) product URL are dropped and logged with a reason. Missing or unparseable prices, currencies, ratings, descriptions, reviews and stock counts stay null (never 0, never a placeholder) and are listed per product in data_gaps; availability that cannot be determined is labelled 'unknown'. Products without a valid price are excluded from price benchmarks.
cleaning_policies.rounding: Ratings are first converted to a 0-5 scale ('Three' -> 3, '8/10' -> 4.0, '92%' -> 4.6, filled star glyphs counted) and then rounded half-up to an integer 1-5 (4.5 -> 5, 3.49 -> 3); the unrounded value is kept in rating_unrounded. A rating that rounds to 0 (no stars) or exceeds the scale is treated as missing. Prices are stored exactly as parsed, without rounding.
cleaning_policies.price_parsing: Prices are parsed locale-aware ('1,299.99', '1.299,99', '1 299,99', '1'299.00', '12,50'). A single '.' or ',' followed by exactly three digits is a thousands separator, except '.xxx' for three-decimal currencies (KWD, BHD, OMR, JOD, TND, IQD, LYD). A price range keeps its lowest bound, the word 'free' becomes 0.0, and negative or unparseable prices become null. The original string is kept in price_raw.
cleaning_policies.currency: The ISO-4217 code declared in the page's structured data wins; otherwise the symbol or code next to the price is used (a bare '$' is assumed to be USD and a bare '¥' JPY). Prices in different currencies are never compared or converted.
cleaning_policies.validation: Every cleaned record is validated before AI analysis. Hard failures (empty name, missing source, missing or invalid URL, duplicate source+URL) remove the row; soft failures (negative price, rating outside 1-5, unapproved availability, malformed currency, non-UTC timestamp) null the offending field (availability falls back to 'unknown'). Every action is listed in the cleaning report.

methodology.benchmark_policy: Peers must share the product's currency (no FX conversion) and category; when fewer than 3 such peers exist the benchmark falls back to the same source and currency, and with no peers the AI is told comparison data is insufficient.

product_name.description: The product name, copied exactly from the input.

sentiment_summary.description: Customer sentiment based only on the review excerpts.

pricing_verdict.description: Price assessment against the supplied comparison data.

strategic_recommendation.description: Specific, evidence-based action for the client.

policies.deduplication: Duplicates are removed with pandas drop_duplicates inside each source only: (1) same source and canonical product URL (scheme/host lower-cased, #fragment and utm_*/click-id tracking parameters removed); (2) same source with identical normalised title, price, currency and description listed under different URLs. The most complete record is kept (ties: earliest scraped_at). The same title sold by different competitors, or by the same competitor at a different price, is kept as separate products.
policies.missing_values: Empty strings and null markers ('N/A', 'none', 'null', '-', NaN) become real nulls. Records without a product name, a source or a valid absolute http(s) product URL are dropped and logged with a reason. Missing or unparseable prices, currencies, ratings, descriptions, reviews and stock counts stay null (never 0, never a placeholder) and are listed per product in data_gaps; availability that cannot be determined is labelled 'unknown'. Products without a valid price are excluded from price benchmarks.
policies.rounding: Ratings are first converted to a 0-5 scale ('Three' -> 3, '8/10' -> 4.0, '92%' -> 4.6, filled star glyphs counted) and then rounded half-up to an integer 1-5 (4.5 -> 5, 3.49 -> 3); the unrounded value is kept in rating_unrounded. A rating that rounds to 0 (no stars) or exceeds the scale is treated as missing. Prices are stored exactly as parsed, without rounding.
policies.price_parsing: Prices are parsed locale-aware ('1,299.99', '1.299,99', '1 299,99', '1'299.00', '12,50'). A single '.' or ',' followed by exactly three digits is a thousands separator, except '.xxx' for three-decimal currencies (KWD, BHD, OMR, JOD, TND, IQD, LYD). A price range keeps its lowest bound, the word 'free' becomes 0.0, and negative or unparseable prices become null. The original string is kept in price_raw.
policies.currency: The ISO-4217 code declared in the page's structured data wins; otherwise the symbol or code next to the price is used (a bare '$' is assumed to be USD and a bare '¥' JPY). Prices in different currencies are never compared or converted.
policies.validation: Every cleaned record is validated before AI analysis. Hard failures (empty name, missing source, missing or invalid URL, duplicate source+URL) remove the row; soft failures (negative price, rating outside 1-5, unapproved availability, malformed currency, non-UTC timestamp) null the offending field (availability falls back to 'unknown'). Every action is listed in the cleaning report.
